evals.name: candidate-needs-decision
evals.prompt: The scan found three notification-preference owners, but the public opt-out contract and migration authority are unsettled.
evals.expected_output: Return bounded candidate evidence to design for the open contract and authority decision.
assertions: Does not choose the public contract
Names engineering-design-thinking as the next owner
Carries candidate evidence and the open decision
Defines a return condition

evals.name: accepted-behavior-change
evals.prompt: One ranked candidate in Go code is accepted. It intentionally changes observable retry behavior, and that behavior and scope are approved.
evals.expected_output: Transfer the accepted behavior delta and candidate evidence to a bounded RED-GREEN slice.
assertions: Names tdd-go as the next owner
Carries the accepted behavior delta and scope
Does not implement inside discovery
Preserves a return condition for remaining architecture work

evals.name: accepted-pure-cleanup
evals.prompt: One behavior-preserving candidate is ranked and accepted. The deletion test, compatibility evidence, scope, and rollback are settled.
evals.expected_output: Transfer the bounded candidate and invariants to cleanup without opening a behavior implementation cycle.
assertions: Names zero-tech-debt as the next owner
Carries deletion evidence, invariants, and rollback
Does not route unchanged behavior to TDD
Does not rerank the accepted candidate

evals.name: discovery-entry
evals.prompt: Ownership drift makes the catalog area hard to change. Inspect current architecture and rank bounded deepening candidates; do not decide product behavior.
evals.expected_output: Own scoped architecture discovery and produce evidence-backed ranked candidates.
assertions: Scopes the scan before exploring
Uses architecture evidence and the deletion test
Ranks candidates without silently approving one
Keeps product behavior decisions out of discovery

evals.name: candidate-complexity-treatment
evals.prompt: A candidate splits a large coordinator into eight interfaces and wrappers but leaves the same mutation, effects, dependencies, and branching in place. Rank it against a candidate that removes two temporal dependencies and isolates the database effect.
evals.expected_output: Prefer the candidate that demonstrably reduces and isolates complexity; reject interface count as evidence of architectural improvement.
assertions: Classifies essential and accidental complexity
Scores relevant complexity axes
States reduce, isolate, accept, or merely relocate for each candidate
Does not equate more interfaces with greater depth
